children: By Emily Ou Yong

Iron ore futures edged up on Wednesday, continuing to stabilise after last week's sharp fall, as supply disruption in Brazil linked to El Niño provided short-term support, countering a drag from weak Chinese steel mill profitability.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
traded 0.07% higher at 712 yuan ($106.18) a metric ton. Last week it plunged nearly 1%.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was little changed at $96 a ton.
Demand typically strengthens ahead of the Golden Week holiday in top consumer China in October, analysts from ANZ Research said in a note.

Earlier, prices had been weighed down by a strong supply outlook, softer confidence in China's steel demand prospects, and the ramp-up of the Simandou project in Guinea, BMI analysts said in a report.
In major iron ore producer Brazil, El Niño tends to bring heavier-than-usual rainfall, which can disrupt rail transport of ore and slow port loading operations, said a Malaysia-based analyst.
Weak steel mill profitability in China remained a drag.

The blast furnace operating rate among 247 steel mills in China fell 0.8 percentage points week-on-week to 82.32% as of September 22, while capacity utilisation rose 0.5 percentage points to 89.23%, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
Elevated coking coal prices
NYMEX:ACT1!
, which were down 1.67% on the DCE for the day, pressured steel mill margins.
Prices of the steelmaking ingredient climbed to $262 a ton on September 18, up 36.5% year-on-year, as safety inspections and mine suspensions in Shanxi curbed domestic supply, BMI analysts added.
DCE coke (DCJcv1), another steelmaking ingredient, was down 0.93%.
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar
lost 0.26% and hot-rolled coil
fell 0.18%, while stainless steel
rose 0.65%.
($1 = 6.7053 Chinese yuan)
